title: Bollywood's New Dads Took Over Father's Day. The Leading Men Are Posting Diapers, Not Six-Packs Now.
excerpt: Ranveer, Vicky, Sidharth and a teary Karan Deol turned June 21 into the softest day on the Bollywood calendar — and the diaspora WhatsApp groups noticed.
body:
There was a time the Bollywood hero came home from the gym, peeled off his shirt for the camera, and called it a personality. This Father's Day, the same men spent June 21 posting toddlers in their arms and captions about cycles they're trying not to repeat. The leading man has a new accessory, and it's a baby monitor.

Start with Karan Deol, who broke the internet's heart before lunch. The grandson of Dharmendra and son of Sunny Deol posted a note calling his father "my first hero," stitched together with first glimpses from Batwara 1947 — the Rajkumar Santoshi Partition saga that reunites Sunny and Santoshi after three decades and lands August 14. It's a clever bit of timing: a son's tribute doubling as a film promo, and somehow it works, because the affection reads real. The Deol men have always traded in dhai-kilo-ka-haath machismo. Watching one of them go misty over his dad is the kind of plot twist that lands.

Then there's the new dads' club, and it is stacked. Ranveer Singh — the most maximalist man in Hindi cinema, a human disco ball in a sherwani — is now a girl dad to Dua, with a second child on the way with Deepika Padukone. The man who never met a leopard print he didn't love keeps talking, softly, about gratitude. Vicky Kaushal marked his first Father's Day with son Vihaan, the boy he welcomed with Katrina Kaif last year, the child the couple has guarded so fiercely from cameras that paparazzi treat a glimpse like a Cannes premiere. By every insider account, Kaushal is the hands-on one, the dad doing the 3 a.m. shift between shoots.

**"Being a dad." — Filmfare

Sidharth Malhotra is in his first Father's Day too, doting on daughter Saraayah while shooting Vvan, the little girl he and Kiara Advani welcomed last July."**

"Even the biggest stars come home to the same role. Being a dad." — Filmfare

Sidharth Malhotra is in his first Father's Day too, doting on daughter Saraayah while shooting Vvan, the little girl he and Kiara Advani welcomed last July. Randeep Hooda and Lin Laishram named their March-born daughter Nyomica. Rajkummar Rao and Patralekhaa are raising baby Parvati, born on their wedding anniversary, because of course she was. Even Arbaaz Khan is doing fatherhood again after two decades, with baby Sipaara. The maternity-ward energy in B-town this past year has been relentless.

What makes this more than a photo-dump is the shift in posture. The previous generation of Bollywood fathers defined themselves by distance — the strict patriarch, the absent provider, the legend the kids had to live up to. This crop is performing closeness instead. They want you to know they change diapers. They want the soft launch of fatherhood as carefully as they once wanted the abs reveal. Cynics will call it brand management, and they're not entirely wrong. But there's something genuinely new about a generation of male stars deciding that tenderness is an asset, not a leak in the armour.

The women curated the day with the same precision. Ananya Panday flooded her grid with family throwbacks for both her mother Bhavana's birthday and Father's Day, the kind of double-duty post that signals a star who knows exactly how the algorithm — and the aunties — work.

For the diaspora, the timing is almost too neat. Father's Day in the US, UK, Canada and Australia falls on the third Sunday of June, so the NRI WhatsApp groups lit up at the same moment Mumbai did. A second-generation kid in New Jersey scrolling Karan Deol's tribute to Sunny is having a very specific feeling — the one where your dad never said the soft thing out loud, and a movie star just said it for him. That's the real diaspora hook here. These posts travel because they're translatable. You don't need to follow the box office to understand a son calling his father his first hero.

The screen versions are coming, too. Batwara 1947 will give Sunny and Karan Deol a father-son arc in August. Ranveer's next, the Don 3 universe, keeps inching forward. Vicky Kaushal has Mahavatar blocking eighteen months of his calendar. But for one Sunday, the spreadsheet of release dates went quiet, and the most powerful men in Indian cinema agreed to be photographed doing the least glamorous, most universal thing there is. Holding a kid. Looking wrecked with love. Posting it anyway.

Happy Father's Day, B-town. The abs can wait.
